findings.title: Changing the Redis key type breaks buffers created by the previous version
findings.body: This changes `span-buf:s:*` keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without changing the key namespace or migrating existing keys. During a rollout, active keys written by the old version remain sets; `ZADD` here then fails with `WRONGTYPE` (and the Lua script also uses sorted-set commands on these keys). Consumers processing traces with such buffers will fail until the keys expire, stalling ingestion and potentially losing buffered spans.

findings.title: Paginator-specific option is passed to the endpoint pagination helper
findings.body: `enable_advanced_features` is an option on `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, but this call passes it to `self.paginate`. The endpoint pagination helper does not accept or forward this paginator-specific keyword, so an authorized administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` gets a `TypeError` instead of a response. Pass the option through the helper's supported mechanism or construct the paginator with it.

findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint orders by `datetime`, but this implementation uses `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the field value, which is a `datetime`; that raises `TypeError` when `build_cursor` processes a nonempty page. Its `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime, so subsequent-page filtering would fail as well. This paginator needs the datetime cursor encoding used by `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets cause unsupported Django queryset slicing
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly as the start of a queryset slice. Django querysets reject negative slice indices with `ValueError`; `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, so a request containing such a cursor returns a server error rather than a pagination response or a client error.

findings.title: The eviction limit ignores the configured segment span limit
findings.body: Eviction is hard-coded to 1000 here, while `SpansBuffer` exposes `max_segment_spans` as a configurable limit and previously enforced that value when loading segments. The new insertion-time cap no longer honors non-default values, so configurations expecting a lower cap can retain and emit substantially more spans than allowed, while higher configured limits are silently reduced.
